characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2000FX TEM; thin foils prepared by twin-jet electro-polishing in a mixture of 10% perchloric acid and 90% ethanol at 25 V
characterization_methods.key_findings: Nano-sized cuboid κ particles observed in the γ matrix (bright-field image) and disc-like B2 in α at higher temperatures.
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterization of the ordered phases (κ-carbide and B2) in the microstructure
characterization_methods.technique: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM), selected-area diffraction patterns (SADPs) and bright-field (BF) imaging

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Carl Zeiss Sigma FE-SEM operated at 20 kV, fitted with high-speed X-ray EDS
characterization_methods.key_findings: Used to image B2 stringer bands, grain-boundary B2 and γ + κ matrix features at the four annealing temperatures.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens polished and etched in a 5% nital solution
characterization_methods.purpose: Observation of the microstructures and phase morphology
characterization_methods.technique: Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM) with X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Nano-indentation with a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s^-1
characterization_methods.key_findings: Precipitate-bearing composites are markedly harder (~5–10 GPa) than the parent γ and α phases (~3–4 GPa); α + κ (500 °C) = 5.3 GPa and γ + κ (500 °C) = 6.8 GPa in the Ni-free alloy.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Maximum load 10000 μN, hold time 20 s; each phase measured at least 25 times; arrays of 50–70 indentations
characterization_methods.purpose: Measurement of nano-hardness of individual phases (γ, α, B2 stringer bands, micrometer- and nano-disk B2) and of phase combinations (γ+κ, α+κ, γ+B2, α+B2, γ+κ+B2)

analytical_models.equation_role: C11 from longitudinal velocity v_l[100]=sqrt(C11/ρ) and C44 from transverse velocity v_t[100]=sqrt(C44/ρ); C12 from v_l[111]=sqrt((C11+2C12+4C44)/(3ρ))
analytical_models.model_note: Acoustic-branch slopes along [100] and [111] used to extract cubic elastic constants.

analytical_models.equation_role: Volume-conserving orthorhombic distortion E(δ)=E(0)+(C11−C12)Vδ²+O(δ⁴) to obtain C11 and C12; monoclinic distortion E(δ)=E(0)+½C44Vδ²+O(δ⁴) to obtain C44
analytical_models.model_note: Second independent method used to derive Cij for the compounds.
Used to compute bulk modulus, anisotropy factor, shear modulus and directional Young's moduli listed in Table 4.

analytical_models.equation_role: Δτ ∝ R^−1.25 (increase in shear stress inversely proportional to precipitate diameter)
analytical_models.model_note: Used to rationalize higher hardness from nano-sized disk-like B2 particles in the α matrix.

analytical_models.equation_role: Fitting of unit-cell volume vs energy to calculate the bulk modulus
analytical_models.model_note: Various unit cell volumes simulated and fitted with the Murnaghan equation of state.

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Structure optimization with Brillouin-zone integration on an 18 × 18 × 18 Monkhorst-Pack grid; real-space grid with 50 Ryd energy cut-off for charge density; augmentation charges expanded to 600 Ryd; 30 × 30 × 30 grid with 60 Ryd cut-off for electronic DOS and formation-energy calculations; density of states via tetrahedron method on a 30 × 30 × 30 mesh
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: GGA of Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) in spin-polarized manner; ultrasoft pseudo-potentials created with a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated lattice parameter of ordered FeAl-B2 with/without spin effects was slightly less than the experimental value but in good agreement with reported experimental values; lattice constant of Fe3AlC calculated larger than Fe3Al-L12, agreeing with experiments.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: nanoindentation hardness of B2-bearing / κ-bearing structures

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental alloys were melted in an induction furnace.
Solution heat-treated for 35 min at 1250 °C in a protective argon atmosphere and then water quenched.
The materials were cut into 3-mm (length), 3-mm (width) and 1-mm (thickness) samples.
Annealing treatments were conducted at 500, 700, 900 and 1050 °C; the holding time is not explicitly reported in the text.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Nano-indentation at a constant loading/unloading rate of 500 μN s^-1 up to a maximum load of 10000 μN with a hold time of 20 s; each phase measured at least 25 times in arrays of 50–70 indentations.

hardness.region: γ + κ (composite of austenite with cuboid κ-carbide), 500 °C
α + κ (composite of ferrite with needle-like κ-carbide), 500 °C

precipitates.distribution: nano-sized blocks formed in the austenite (γ) phase
coarse B2 particles in the γ matrix (and grain boundaries)
micron-sized needle-like particles within the ferrite (α) phase; average size ≈1.5 μm

structures.overall_structure: Duplex γ + α matrix. γ matrix contains nano-sized cuboid κ-carbide blocks (< 100 nm) and coarse FeAl-type B2 particles (2–4 μm); α (ferrite) contains needle-like κ-carbide (width 200 ± 33 nm). At 500 °C the Ni-free sample shows α + needle-like κ-carbides instead of the B2 stringer bands seen in the Ni-containing sample.

unmapped_findings: Solution-treated reference hardness for the Ni-free Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C alloy (parent state of this 500 °C sample): γ = 4 GPa and α = 3 GPa (Table 2; b0034).
Mn content of κ-carbide in the Ni-free alloy annealed at 500 °C: ≈18.4 wt.% Mn in the α + κ composite and 20.4 wt.% Mn in the γ + κ composite (Fig. 4f, Fig. 4h; b0029).
At low annealing temperatures (500–700 °C) this Ni-free alloy exhibited low ductility, with elongation ≈10% (b0014).
Annealing holding time for the 500 °C treatment is not explicitly reported in the text (b0017).

The Ni-free alloy is denoted Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C throughout the abstract/introduction/methods/conclusions but is labelled Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C in Tables 1 and 2, an apparent typographical inconsistency (0.5 vs 0.8 C).
